title: Cohere moves to buy AI cybersecurity startup Aisle By Reuters
key_facts: Toronto-based Cohere signed a letter of intent to acquire Prague-based Aisle; financial terms not disclosed
Aisle, founded in 2024, builds AI systems that detect and help address software vulnerabilities
Aisle says it found more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities in more than 100 code bases in the past year and matched or beat competing systems
Cohere will combine Aisle's autonomous security research with its models and invest substantially in Prague as a global hub for AI cybersecurity
Aisle co-founders get roles in a new Cohere Cyber division
Earlier this year Cohere bought Reliant AI and announced a combination with Aleph Alpha, which needs regulatory approval
quote_evidence: Toronto-based Cohere said on Thursday that it had signed a letter of intent to acquire Aisle, which is based in Prague. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Aisle said it had found more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities in more than 100 code bases in the past year, and said its platform has matched or outperformed competing systems.
Cohere also said it will make a substantial investment in Prague.
why_it_matters_hint: AI firms are buying cyber-defence skill as AI both finds and exploits software flaws.
notes: Investing.com page blocked (403); read The Globe and Mail, which did its own reporting. Reuters also carried the story. Aisle performance claims are company claims.
